messages:
Priya (oncall): seeing increased packet loss from az1c GPU hosts, tx drops spiking ~15% since 08:12 UTC. some inference pods reporting KV cache write timeouts. autoscaler started killing pods -> flapping. anyone already on this?
InfraBot: ALERT: network.loss.az1c >= 12% for 5m. affected clusters: rl-infer-prod-gpu, rl-batch-gpu. LB 5xx rate +3.2x.
Ajay: on it. grabbing netlogs and looking at BGP peering. initial read: asymmetric egress causing retransmits to GPU hosts.
Zoe: can we avoid mass evictions? draining will cause cold-starts and extra cost for recovery. prefer to steer new traffic away and keep existing pods alive while we stabilize.
Priya (oncall): agreed. plan: 1) steer /proxy weight off az1c for new requests, 2) disable horizontal autoscaler to stop evictions, 3) run small cache warmers in target AZs, 4) cordon most-affected nodes and drain last-resort. Assign: Ajay -> proxy/LB, Zoe -> warmers, Sam -> monitor SLOs.
Ajay: updating envoy weights now. command: curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/v1/lb/adjust -d '{"region":"us-west-2","zone":"az1c","weight":0.1}' (will keep tiny weight for sticky sessions).
Sam: watching token latency and 99p tail. setting alerts to page if 99p > 2s. also pausing autoscaler with: kubectl -n infra patch hpa infer-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4,"maxReplicas":4}}'
Zoe: prepping warmers, will spin up 6 warm instances in az1a/az1b and prepopulate model KV cache + prefix caches. snippet: for i in 1..6; do ./cache_warmer --model gpt-xl --target az1a; done
Danny: cost note: warming 6 instances and holding extra capacity for ~30m adds ~0.6 GPU-hours; cheaper than repeated cold starts + retries. ok with tradeoff.
Ajay: envoy weight change pushed. proxy metrics show new request distribution shifting off az1c -> az1a/az1b within 18s.
InfraBot: INFO: weight.adj.us-west-2.az1c -> 0.1 by ajay at 08:24:05 UTC.
Sam: autoscaler patched to fixed replica count. no further evictions in last 3m.
Zoe: warmers started. KV hit-rate in az1a/az1b up from 6% -> 72% within first 2m.
Priya (oncall): good. next: cordon the worst nodes but hold drains unless we confirm degraded NICs. Ajay, can you collect dmesg + ethtool on node-07 and node-11?
Ajay: pulling logs: node-07 NIC errors increasing, suspect firmware offload regression. sending to hw team and marking node-07 cordoned (kubectl cordon node-07). command: kubectl cordon node-07
Sam: routing stable, 99p down from 3.8s -> 1.1s. error budget burn paused.
Zoe: skip drain for node-11 for now; keep pods as-is but set max_surge for deployments to 0 to avoid recreations.
Danny: tagging this change in the cost tracker and notifying finance for temporary capacity bump.
Priya (oncall): summary: we've shifted new traffic away, paused autoscaling, warmed caches in healthy AZs, cordoned one bad node. next steps: hardware team to confirm NIC regression; if confirmed -> drain and decommission node-07; else uncordon and restore weights. keep monitoring for 30m. thanks team. :thumbsup:
Ajay: noted. ping me if anything flips.
Sam: monitoring dashboard pinned in this thread. will update every 5m.
InfraBot: RESOLVE_CHECK: after 25m, network.loss.az1c dropped to 2.1%. current weight.az1c = 0.1.
Priya (oncall): if loss stays <3% for 15m, we will gradually restore weight to 1.0. marking incident state: mitigated.
Zoe: warmers will run for another 10m then scale down.
Danny: cost estimate ~0.9 GPU-hours additional during mitigation window.
Priya (oncall): great. closing loop later with postmortem if root cause confirmed. thanks.
